text:
sam_w: Heads up — after the packer refactor deployed last night we're seeing ~12% p95 latency regression for prefix-heavy workloads. Flamegraphs point at frequent kernel switches during prefill merging (quantized vs fp16 path). I grabbed a few traces and a short log snippet below.

leah: Can you paste one of the traces? rough sample is fine. is this isolated to a region/shard? @miguel any ideas from profiling?

sam_w: sample trace:
```
prefill: segments=[contig(128),hit(64),contig(32)]
packer.coalesce: merged=3->1 (virtual_len=224)
kernel_selector: choose quant4 -> choose fp16_fused -> back to quant4 (within 30ms)
perf: microbatch_generate_ms spike at 95th
```
Observed on e2 shards handling chat-like traffic (shard-22/shard-24).

miguel: I instrumented the packer locally this morning. Root cause looks like the coalesce policy merging non-contiguous prefills + hit fragments into a single virtual length. The packer then sets a virtual_length that crosses the knob thresholds in kernel_selector leading to oscillation. Also if the KV-cache hit fragments are interleaved, the runtime ends up switching to a different kernel optimized for longer sequences mid-microbatch.

toni: Proposed quick fixes: 1) prefer coalescing only contiguous prefill segments above a threshold, 2) scale token_budget_target by hit_ratio (more hits -> lower budget so we don't inadvertently grow virtual_length), 3) add short kernel_stability_window to avoid switching kernels within N ms unless >X tokens diff.

sam_w: bench with local canary: token_budget_scale_by_hit=true + contiguous-only coalesce reduced p95 regression from +12% to +3% on the perf harness. Not perfect but promising. Need prod canary.

infra-bot: deploy: canary started on shard-22 with feature flag prefill-coalesce-v2. build: runtime-2026.3.14-canary.

leah: Add these telemetry hooks before broad rollout: kernel_selection_histogram, kernel_switch_count per trace, microbatch_virtual_length, prefill_fragment_count. Also tag traces with feature flag.

miguel: Another edge we saw: client cancellations (short-circuit) cause prefill fragments to be left behind and later merged with new requests — increases fragmentation. I'm going to add a sticky-prefill TTL (200ms) so prefill fragments evict early unless coalesced contiguously.

sam_w: I'll schedule the canary and prepare an eval set of prompt prefixes that maximize cache-hit skew. Also adding a fallback: if kernel_switch_count > 2 within 50ms then force fallback to "stable_kernel" for that microbatch and emit alert.

toni: I'll open the PR with unit tests for packer merging and a small perf harness to simulate fragmentation churn. Will also add a config snippet: 
```
{"prefill_coalesce_threshold":"0.8",
 "prefill_contiguous_only":true,
 "token_budget_scale_by_hit":true,
 "kernel_stability_window_ms":20,
 "sticky_prefill_ttl_ms":200,
 "kernel_switch_fallback_threshold":2}
```

sam_w: sounds good. Next steps: run canary for 6h, collect kernel_switch_count and p95 delta, and then decide rollback vs full rollout. Thanks all :rocket:

leah: also add a perf regression test to CI that simulates 70%+ kv-hit ratio traffic with alternating small & large prefills. That was what exposed this.

miguel: noted. will add synthetic harness and a short-run profiler to capture kernel metrics.

infra-bot: alert: canary shard-22 initial 30m metrics: p95 +2.7% vs baseline, kernel_switch_rate down 60% on flagged traces. Monitoring for next 5h.

sam_w: Nice — keep the metrics coming, we'll reconvene after the 6h window. Thanks everyone.
